objective: Design a local dependency-light text indexing CLI before implementation.

portfolio_reference.evidence: Invented reference shapes exercise the comparison schema; no real project inventory or source retrieval is claimed.

portfolio_assessments.objective_specific_fit: Its dependency-light local Python boundary fits the proposed CLI objective.
portfolio_assessments.solo_maintenance_cost: Reuses an already familiar runtime and test path with no new service.

portfolio_assessments.objective_specific_fit: A web application boundary does not serve the local-only first slice.
portfolio_assessments.solo_maintenance_cost: Would add frontend/server/runtime maintenance without an objective need.

portfolio_assessments.objective_specific_fit: The first slice has no boundary that benefits from combining the two baselines.
portfolio_assessments.solo_maintenance_cost: Would create two stack surfaces for one local behavior.

challenge_dispositions.response: Target runtime capability is now an explicit constraint and revisit trigger before the no-package choice can hold.

decision.stack: One local CLI package with explicit file and JSON boundaries
decision.tooling: unittest with no required third-party package
architecture: Pure indexing logic behind a small command adapter.
Input and output stay local and deterministic.
No service, database, or network dependency in the first slice.

alternatives.option: Add an application framework and persistent database at kickoff
alternatives.reason_not_selected: The objective has no observed service or persistence requirement.

constraints: Implementation and package installation require a later explicit authorization.
The target runtime must prove the required standard-library capability before the no-package decision holds.
risks: Large inputs may later require performance evidence and a revisited storage choice.
revisit_triggers: A measured input size fails the accepted local performance boundary.
A real consumer requires a network API or shared persistence.
The authorized target runtime lacks a required standard-library capability.
